title: Feeling the beat: Baby Dodds and others
summary: Taylor says a drummer must feel the beat and praises Dodds, Baby Hall, Zutty and Gene Cooper.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: the beat, but you give him another beat with the other hand.
I've tried to do it. I tried to get him to show me, and he'd show me with the same thing.
Yeah, I know what you mean.

And another thing about it, I think that a drummer must have what I call, he must feel the beat, feeling the beat. You can always tell a drummer when he feels the beat. Baby Dodds was a man who felt the beat. His whole body responded to the rhythms. He would shimmy and rock and both feet going and press by, and it was just wonderful to watch.
He always seemed so happy. Always had that smile on his face.

And everything was his own. It came out of his own head. I don't think he patterned after anyone. And I used to tell him I'm going to have a lot of fun with him, and I told him I was going to make a musical bed spring. He said, well let me see it. And there was, Baby Hall was a famous five-stroke old man. He did it perfect. He was a good timekeeper, and I think that his, he was another one who could feel the beat. I believe Zutty could feel the beat. He just got to feel it. I've seen a lot of great drummers who were just, had a great technique on the drums, and could do many tricks, and all sorts of rhythm, but they just couldn't feel the beat. They just, they just play along with the band, but they never could excite anyone. And I think that I can feel the beat a little bit, but not much as Baby Hall.
I'm sure you can. Baby admired you, I know, a lot. He told me that several times.
And I want to give a lot of credit to Gene Cooper. That's another boy can feel the beat. I think it goes all over.
